1.title: Marl-Limestone Group (Part 2)
1.items.0.label: Mambourg (Sigolsheim, 61.85 ha)
1.items.0.desc: Due south-facing and one of the plots with the longest sunshine hours, calcium-magnesium soil under a Tertiary conglomerate marl cover. Its reputation is recorded as early as 783. Low yields, mainly Gewurztraminer, with elegant flavours and great ageing potential.
1.items.1.label: Mandelberg (Mittelwihr & Beblenheim, 22 ha)
1.items.1.desc: The "almond slope" — Tertiary conglomerate marl-limestone on the edge of the Rhine graben. Farmed since Gallo-Roman times and labelled under its own name since 1925. Gewurztraminer (40%) + Riesling (30%), with prominent fruit, delicacy and elegance, and good ageing strength.
1.items.2.label: Marckrain (Bennwihr & Sigolsheim, 53.35 ha)
1.items.2.desc: Oligocene littoral conglomerate, marl-limestone dominated by oolitic limestone gravel. Documented as early as 777. Gewurztraminer is king, with a powerful structure and complex aromas; Pinot Gris is delicate and reserved yet intensely aromatic.
1.items.3.label: Moenchberg (Andlau & Eichhoffen, 11.83 ha)
1.items.3.desc: The "monks' mountain" — Quaternary dissolution deposits, fine clay soil. Planted in Roman times and owned by the Benedictine abbey of Altdorf in 1097. Mainly Riesling, with elegant varietal character, a solid body and pleasing vitality.
1.items.4.label: Sonnenglanz (Beblenheim, 32.80 ha)
1.items.4.desc: "Sunshine" — Tertiary conglomerate marl, with annual rainfall below 500 mm. Mainly Pinot Gris / Gewurztraminer, with golden colour, ripe intense aromas, and a warm, balanced palate with a long finish.
1.items.5.label: Steingrubler (Wettolsheim, 22.95 ha)
1.items.5.desc: Marl-limestone to clayey-sandy, the sandier upper part suiting Riesling and the lime-rich lower part better suited to Gewurztraminer. Remains of a 13th-century quarry are recorded. Wines have strong ageing potential, rich aromas and a firm structure.
2.title: Clay-Marl: A Heavy, Water-Retentive Cradle of Noble Rot
2.html: The clay-marl (argilo-marneux) family has 5 Grand Crus, with heavy, strongly water-retentive soils, and is one of the most important terroir foundations for Alsace's VT and SGN noble-rot sweet wines.
3.title: The Five Clay-Marl Stars
3.items.0.label: Schoenenbourg (Riquewihr & Zellenberg, 53.40 ha)
3.items.0.desc: Keuper marl / dolomite / gypsum, rich in fertile elements and strongly water-retentive. Famous across Europe from the 16th century; in 1663 the Swiss cartographer Merian praised it as "the noblest wine of the region", and Voltaire once owned several parcels of vineyard here! Riesling is king, and the microclimate is especially suited to VT / SGN noble-rot sweet wines.
3.items.1.label: Kanzlerberg (Bergheim, 3.23 ha)
3.items.1.desc: The smallest Grand Cru in all Alsace! Heavy clayey limestone, grey / black gypsum Keuper marl plus Muschelkalk limestone at the base. Documented by the Knights of Malta in 1312 (already vinified separately). Riesling is especially outstanding, with Pinot Gris / Gewurztraminer also fine, needing long ageing to show the power and breadth given by its heavy terroir.
3.items.2.label: Sporen (Riquewihr, 23.70 ha)
3.items.2.desc: Lias clay-marl with a decalcified surface layer and an unusually high phosphoric acid content — a mark of early ripening and high quality. Recorded in the archives of the Duke of Württemberg in 1432, and praised by Fischart in 1580 as "the first of all Alsace wines". Mainly Gewurztraminer / Pinot Gris, delicate and noble, combining richness and elegance.
3.items.3.label: Froehn (Zellenberg, 14.60 ha)
3.items.3.desc: Lias clay-marl, dark grey shaly marl interbedded with thin layers of white limestone. Gewurztraminer / Pinot Gris / Muscat, with abundant fruit, a full body and excellent ageing potential.
3.items.4.label: Altenberg de Bergbieten (Bergbieten, 29.07 ha)
3.items.4.desc: Gypsum Keuper clay-marl plus dolomite gravel. Mentioned in archives related to Pope Leo IX in 1050. Riesling / Gewurztraminer dominate, with delicate, gentle floral notes and, after several years' ageing, the mellow aromas typical of clay-marl.
4.question: What is special about Kanzlerberg (Bergheim) among the 51 Grand Crus?
4.options.0: It is the largest Grand Cru
4.options.1: It is the smallest Grand Cru in all Alsace, only 3.23 ha
4.options.2: It is the only clay-marl site in Haut-Rhin
4.options.3: It is the most recently delimited Grand Cru
4.explanation: Kanzlerberg covers only 3.23 ha, the smallest of Alsace's 51 Grand Crus. As early as 1312, documents of the Knights of Malta record "separate vinification" (vinification séparée) of the vineyard here, proving its outstanding quality was recognised from the Middle Ages.
5.message: Marl-limestone group (Part 2) and clay-marl complete! You now know all 51 Grand Cru sites!
5.keyPoints.0: Mambourg, Mandelberg, Marckrain, Moenchberg, Sonnenglanz and Steingrubler complete the 13 marl-limestone sites
5.keyPoints.1: The clay-marl family (5 sites) has heavy, water-retentive soils, an important terroir foundation for VT / SGN noble-rot sweet wines
5.keyPoints.2: Schoenenbourg (53.40 ha): Voltaire once owned vineyards here, king of Riesling, an ideal origin for VT / SGN
5.keyPoints.3: Kanzlerberg (3.23 ha): the smallest Grand Cru in all Alsace, with separate vinification recorded as early as 1312
5.keyPoints.4: Sporen: praised in 1580 as "the first of all Alsace wines"
